description: Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In mathematics, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiralling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents and pineapples.

copyright: Icebergs, Ilulissat, Greenland (© James Yu/Getty Images)
description: Off Greenland's west coast, enormous icebergs drift through the cold waters, creating a landscape that's constantly changing. Many originate from the nearby Jakobshavn Glacier, one of the world's fastest and most active glaciers. The surrounding Ilulissat Icefjord, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lies about 250 kilometres north of the Arctic Circle. Here, towering blocks of ice break away and begin their slow journey towards the open sea, forming one of Greenland's most remarkable natural sights.

copyright: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France (© Siripong Kaewla-iad/Getty Images)
description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by ancient Greeks and long connected to the Italian royal House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, that layered past remains visible throughout the coastal city in the south of France, where old-world architecture meets the blue Mediterranean waters and sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.

copyright: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway (© Espen Bergersen/Minden Pictures)
description: Off the coast of Kvaløya in Troms, Northern Norway, humpback whales move through the cold Arctic waters in search of a proper feast. They visit this region during the winter months, following migrating herring into the fjords. Humpbacks are famous for bubble-net feeding, a remarkable hunting technique in which whales blow rings of bubbles to corral fish before lunging upwards, open-mouthed, to catch their prey. In today's image, a humpback slips beneath the icy waves under a glowing pastel sky, capturing a moment of tranquility in Norway's wild north.

copyright: Coast redwoods near Melbourne, Victoria, Australia (© James Yu/Getty Images)
description: Step into this peaceful redwood forest in Victoria, Australia, and the outside world can suddenly feel very far away. Coast redwoods (Sequoia sempervirens) tower overhead, forming a leafy canopy above the forest floor. These impressive trees have grown into one of the region's most distinctive woodland sights. With their tall trunks, deep green foliage and tranquil surroundings, the redwoods create an inviting place to wander, slow down and enjoy the quiet beauty of the forest.

copyright: Pair of barn owls (© Zahoor Salmi/Getty Images)
description: These barn owls, bathed in evening light, are waiting for the hunt to begin. As night falls, these birds of prey swoop into action, listening for tiny movements in grass or leaves made by mice and voles. Their heart-shaped faces help funnel sound into some of the sharpest ears in the animal kingdom. This allows them to locate their prey with pinpoint precision in the dark before swooping silently, their soft feathers muffling their approach. In autumn, young barn owls strike out to find their own territories. As the nights grow longer, you might spot them earlier in the evening, gliding over fields in search of supper.

copyright: Trail of the Cedars, Glacier National Park, Montana, USA (© DBushue Photography/Getty Images)
description: Sometimes, the best way to clear your head is to step outside. Today's image features the Trail of the Cedars, part of more than 1,100 kilometres of hiking trails in Glacier National Park, Montana, in the northwestern USA. Its 1.4-kilometre loop includes a raised boardwalk that cuts a path through western red cedar and hemlock trees. The park boasts routes for all abilities, taking in alpine lakes, wildflower meadows, mountain passes and wilderness stretching to the Canadian border.
